Subject: Weekly fleet scouting and commit sync — Apr 20

Team,

Quick note ahead of today’s weekly: Orion Labs (Aisha cc'd) is moving toward a pilot close in late May. Sales forecast (hubspot RD-4721) shows a likely start-of-production in July with a front-loaded ramp for the first six weeks. We need a practical mapping from that ramp to pool slots and a short contingency plan if initial benchmarks require higher throughput.

Ask for this thread:
- Infra: confirm available slot types and any fragmentation that would block a mid-May ramp
- Finance: sanity-check the burn profile for a transient two-week burst that exceeds reserved capacity by ~30%
- Sales/CS: confirm the target SLOs that Orion expects for the pilot (latency and concurrency).

Attached: capacity_matcher_q2.xlsx (initial model), commit_timeline.md (draft asks for reserved vs burst windows). I sketched two scenarios in the sheet: conservative reserve (pin 8xA100-equivalents for 12 weeks) and staged-reserve + burst (reserve 4x + burst credits).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Kimberly: call out any pool constraints and recommended GPU shape for consistent latency (e.g., A100s vs H100s)
2) Ben: estimate incremental monthly burn for the staged plan and call out where we might need a temporary credit or price flexibility
3) Laura: note if there are any larger pipeline deals overlapping that should take precedence for mid-May to July window

I’ll summarize and send an updated one-pager before the 2pm bridge.

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the summary, Mateo. A few quick infra notes after a read of the workbook:

- Pool inventory: we have fragmentation in two regions (us-west1 / us-east1) where A100 pools are ~70% utilized by long-running Dedicated commitments. We have short windows of contiguous A100 capacity starting 5/18 and 6/02 (approx). H100 capacity is scarcer but available as burst in us-west1 only.
- Recommendation: for Orion’s pilot, pick an A100-equivalent profile (we can quantify VFLOPs) but plan initial performance benchmarks on the H100 burst path — that gives headroom for latency SLOs without full reserve.
- KV-cache and batching: if their traffic is chat-heavy we should enable prefix caching on the front 8 tokens and a conservative batching window (50ms) to keep latency predictable — I put notes in pool_heatmap_v2.png.
- Risk: fragmentation means we cannot promise contiguous 8xA100-equivalents on May 1. If they need that exact shape we must either: 1) shift start to 5/18 or 2) accept mixed-shape (A100+H100) and validate perf.

I’ll be on the 2pm bridge with a screenshot of the allocation windows.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Infrastructure Capacity Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: pool_heatmap_v2.png
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha@orionlabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 13:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet scouting and commit sync — Apr 20

Thanks — a few finance notes after a quick pass of the scenarios in capacity_matcher_q2.xlsx:

- Conservative reserve (8x A100-eq for 12 weeks): estimated incremental cost to Orion ~ $120k/mo; for Redwood that implies reserved revenue and a modest increase in committed utilization by mid-July.
- Staged-reserve + burst: reserve 4x + burst credits yields an estimated start-month cost of $58k with a 30% uplift in month 2 if benchmarks drive higher throughput.
- Credit ask: If Orion requests temporary burst credits for the first two weeks of production to smooth benchmarking risk, we can propose a $30k one-time credits package tied to acceptance criteria (latency <= 120ms p95 and token costs within 20% of modeled).

Operationally, two things I need from infra to finalize: 1) a deterministic list of swap windows (exact dates where contiguous pools exist) and 2) a likely per-hour burn for the H100 fallback so I can model the credit economics.

If we align on the staged plan, I can prepare a conditional invoice template that ties credits to the acceptance criteria above and routes approvals through Sales Ops.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Perfect — appreciate the quick turn. Short summary and action items to keep cadence tight:

Summary (agreed):
- Path: staged-reserve + burst credits (reserve 4x A100-eq + H100 burst fallback in us-west1)
- Pricing: Ben to draft conditional invoice with $30k one-time credits tied to p95 latency <=120ms and token-cost variance <=20%
- Schedule: infra to confirm contiguous window dates (Kimby note: target windows 5/18 and 6/02; need exact hours)

Action items:
- Kimberly: add exact start/end time windows for the 5/18 and 6/02 contiguous capacity blocks and provide per-hour burn estimate for H100 fallback (due EOD Wed 4/22).
- Ben: prepare conditional invoice and credit language; include approval route and expiration (due Thu 4/23).
- Laura: flag any higher-priority pipeline conflicts that must be considered before we lock windows (due EOD Tue 4/21).
- Mateo: update capacity_matcher_q2.xlsx with final numbers after infra and finance inputs and share a 1-page summary for the execs.

Aisha — appreciate you joining the thread. If the staged-reserve option looks viable at your end, we can circulate the conditional invoice and sync procurement timelines.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the 2pm bridge and attach the updated one-pager after Kim and Ben post their inputs.

Cheers,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
